solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: He gives gun up on entering

indicators.note: the word on goes into the middle of the reversed gun
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: rod is American slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A man fires a gun as he comes in through a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He gives' is the definition; 'up' works because this is a down entry, read from the bottom, and 'entering' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A donor is a person who gives, such as blood or money to a charity.

clue.text: Relieved the head cold came to an end

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, here of the word cold

parts.note: relieved, of pain, means eased

explanation.surface: Someone's headache and cold cleared up and stopped bothering them.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cease is to stop or finish, so ceased means stopped.

clue.text: He aims to be boss

definitions.meaning: a person who directs or points something at a target, read literally
the person in charge of a company or a film

explanation.surface: An ambitious man sets his sights on being in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: One who directs aims things, and a company director is a boss.

clue.text: Love the French sweetheart — his squeeze!

parts.note: cher is French for dear, a term for a sweetheart

indicators.note: squeezing the word his crushes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman's sweetheart embraces her lovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the French' signals a French word: cher means dear. 'squeeze' is the anagram signal, not a hug.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to cherish someone is to love and treasure them.

clue.text: Left to travel abroad right after — the dog!

indicators.note: right comes after the other pieces
the letters of abroad travel around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaves home to go abroad and then remembers the family dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to travel' is the anagram signal and 'after' places the right at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A Labrador is a breed of retriever, a common example of a dog.

clue.text: Not the same if fellow is in rented out accommodation

indicators.note: the word if and the fellow go inside the rearranged letters
the rearranged letters accommodate, or house, the other pieces
out, as in worked out, says the letters of rented are rearranged

explanation.surface: Renting out a place is a different matter when a lodger moves in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' is the anagram signal; 'is in' and 'accommodation' both say the inserted pieces are housed, landing after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something different is unlike another, not identical to it.

clue.text: Scrap metals are hoarded in anticipation

indicators.note: the metals are stored away inside the scrap

parts.note: a scrap is a fight
ores are the rocks metals are mined from

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles scrap metal expecting prices to rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: foresight is planning ahead in expectation of what will come.

clue.text: Docking animal's tail, anyhow, is madness

indicators.note: anyhow means in any old order, so the letters are rearranged
docking a tail is cutting it short, so a letter is lost
the tail of the word is its last letter

parts.note: the word animal, the possessive adding no letter

explanation.surface: Cutting off an animal's tail is crazy in any circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docking' and 'tail' drop the last L from ANIMAL, leaving ANIMA, which 'anyhow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: mania is a state of wild, frenzied madness.

clue.text: Stake goes up — it's high and dangerous

indicators.note: in a down clue going up reads the word from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: the ante is a stake in poker

explanation.surface: A gambler raises the stakes on a risky bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is a tall active volcano in Sicily, lofty and perilous.

clue.text: Finding much worse damage within, give up

indicators.note: the phrase is damaged internally, its letters jumbled

parts.note: far worse means much worse

explanation.surface: Discovering the internal damage is far worse, someone abandons the project.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to forswear something is to renounce or abandon it.

clue.text: Is leaving this hole for the plant

indicators.note: the word is departs from the word this

parts.note: a rift is a split or opening

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a hole dug for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes IS out of THIS, leaving TH.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrift, also called sea pink, is a flowering plant of coasts.

clue.text: Get ready to go to bed

definitions.text: Get ready to go to bed

parts.words: Get ready to go to bed
parts.note: in newspapers, putting a page to bed sends it to press, and copy is prepared first

explanation.surface: Someone prepares for the night's sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Bed here is the printer's sense: a paper goes to bed when it goes to press.
explanation.definitionFit: Editing prepares copy so the newspaper can be sent off for printing.

clue.text: Mean to give support

definitions.meaning: an upright post or pole that holds something up

explanation.surface: Someone intends to offer help.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a norm or average, and also an upright supporting pole.

clue.text: Watch while no sound is heard

parts.note: a while is a period of time

indicators.note: the word for quiet is said aloud, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: peace is quiet, the absence of noise

explanation.surface: Stand guard while silence reigns.
explanation.definitionFit: A wristwatch is one kind of clock, a portable device for telling the hour.

clue.text: Bird attacked smaller one…

parts.note: bit, past tense of bite, means attacked
a tern is a smaller seabird

explanation.surface: A large bird set upon a smaller one.
explanation.definitionFit: A bittern is a marsh-dwelling heron known for its booming call.

clue.text: Charm that well-cut tails give to a fellow

indicators.note: the letters of tails are cut up and reshaped

parts.note: a man is a fellow

explanation.surface: A smartly tailored tailcoat gives a man charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a talisman is a lucky charm or amulet.

clue.text: …with bird left out gazing

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is removed

parts.note: the starling is a common bird

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a bird left out of the flock looks on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: staring means looking fixedly, much like gazing.

clue.text: Be inclined to rely, foolishly and lovingly

parts.note: to tend to do something is to be inclined to it

indicators.note: the letters of rely are arranged in a silly way

explanation.surface: Someone tends to depend on others, unwisely but with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: tenderly means gently and affectionately, with care.

clue.text: Locum suitable for some hole-in-the-wall place?

definitions.meaning: a temporary stand-in, such as a doctor covering for another
fit to block a gap in a wall, read literally

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor suits a tiny back-street surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute, and literally something that plugs a gap.

clue.text: Dead keen, then, goes off to ring the silly bell!

indicators.note: the scrambled word encircles the other piece
going off, like a bad egg, the word then is scrambled
the letters of bell are arranged in a silly way

explanation.surface: Very eager, someone sets off to ring a ridiculous bell.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'goes off' for then and 'silly' for bell; 'to ring' makes the first surround the second, after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: hell-bent means utterly determined, recklessly eager.

clue.text: On leaving one, say worriedly 'Steady on there!'

indicators.note: the word on departs from the word one
the letters of say are fretted into a new order

explanation.surface: As one person leaves, another anxiously urges calm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes ON from ONE, leaving E; 'worriedly' rearranges SAY into ASY.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation 'Easy!' is a call to calm down or go carefully.

clue.text: Who tempted you to steal?

definitions.meaning: A name for the Devil, the tempter
British slang for to pinch or pilfer

explanation.surface: An accusing question: who led you into theft?
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is the Devil, and in British slang to nick is to steal.

clue.text: Reckons it matters

definitions.meaning: is significant, as in every vote is important

explanation.surface: Someone thinks something is important.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to tally up or reckon, and also to be of importance.

clue.text: Put in our hands, coped with

definitions.meaning: handed out, as cards are to players

explanation.surface: Something given to us that we then managed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards are dealt into players' hands, and a problem dealt with is one handled.

clue.text: She won an American beauty competition and got married

definitions.text: She won an American beauty competition and got married

parts.words: She won an American beauty competition and got married
parts.note: the winner of the American pageant; once wed she becomes a wife

explanation.surface: A pageant winner's story: crowned, then married.
explanation.walkthrough: Missus is informal British for wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A married woman is informally someone's missus, playing on the title Miss US.

clue.text: Supposed to be super resort by the sea

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters of super are rearranged

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: A seaside resort is supposedly superb.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: presumed means assumed or supposed to be true.

clue.text: Spat 'Rubbish!'

definitions.meaning: discarded waste, or a verb to dismiss as worthless

explanation.surface: Someone snapped out a dismissive retort.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a brief fight or tiff, and scrap is also waste material.

clue.text: An after-dinner speech?

parts.note: not one formal address but the chat round the dining table

explanation.surface: A formal address given once a meal is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Conversation at the dinner table is informal talk among diners, often after eating.
